transcript.text:
You have two good options depending on your context:

---

## Option 1: Search API (recommended for admins)

The Search API queries Elasticsearch across all identity data, including arbitrary attributes.

```http
POST https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/search/v1
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "indices": ["identities"],
  "query": {
    "query": "attributes.email:jane.doe@example.com"
  }
}
```

You can also use field-specific syntax like the docs show (`attributes.location:austin`) — so for email it would be `attributes.email:jane.doe@example.com`. If you want an exact match with Elasticsearch query syntax you can also try:

```json
{
  "indices": ["identities"],
  "query": {
    "query": "email:\"jane.doe@example.com\""
  }
}
```

**Note:** There is ingestion latency (seconds to minutes) between when identity data changes and when it appears in search results.

---

## Option 2: Public Identities API (non-admin / public attributes)

If email has been configured as a public attribute and you need non-admin access:

```http
GET https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/public-identities/v1?filters=email eq "jane.doe@example.com"
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
```

This is scoped to attributes your org administrator has made publicly visible, so it may not expose all identity data.

---

## Authentication

Get an access token first using Client Credentials:

```bash
curl --location 'https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token' \
  --form 'grant_type="client_credentials"' \
  --form 'client_id="{clientId}"' \
  --form 'client_secret="{clientSecret}"'
```

Then use the returned `access_token` as `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}` in your identity lookup request.

---

```answer-summary
endpoints:
  - method: POST
    path: /search/v1
    api_version: search/v1
  - method: GET
    path: /public-identities/v1
    api_version: public-identities/v1
auth_flow: OAuth2 bearer token (client credentials grant via PAT)
required_scopes: []
key_parameters: [indices, query, filters]
```
